{"newText":"# Providers

See [cli.md](cli.md) for the `/settings` hub and CLI flags.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key, the custom-provider and role
surfaces) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks, overriding the
provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages ONLY when the
declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind — `record anthropic +
wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks still run. The override
silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller asserts the endpoint
speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report (`wire override:`) so
a silenced check is never invisible.

# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"newText":"# Providers

See [cli.md](cli.md) for the `/settings` hub and CLI flags.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key, the custom-provider and role
surfaces) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks, overriding the
provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages ONLY when the
declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind — `record anthropic +
wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks still run. The override
silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller asserts the endpoint
speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report (`wire override:`) so
a silenced check is never invisible.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"newText":"# Providers

See [cli.md](cli.md) for the `/settings` hub and CLI flags.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key, the custom-provider and role
surfaces) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks, overriding the
provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages ONLY when the
declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind — `record anthropic +
wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks still run. The override
silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller asserts the endpoint
speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report (`wire override:`) so
a silenced check is never invisible.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

{"newText":"# Providers

See [cli.md](cli.md) for the `/settings` hub and CLI flags.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key, the custom-provider and role
surfaces) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks, overriding the
provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages ONLY when the
declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind — `record anthropic +
wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks still run. The override
silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller asserts the endpoint
speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report (`wire override:`) so
a silenced check is never invisible.

{"newText":"# Providers

See [cli.md](cli.md) for the `/settings` hub and CLI flags.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key, the custom-provider and role
surfaces) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks, overriding the
provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages ONLY when the
declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind — `record anthropic +
wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks still run. The override
silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller asserts the endpoint
speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report (`wire override:`) so
a silenced check is never invisible.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"newText":"# Providers

See [cli.md](cli.md) for the `/settings` hub and CLI flags.

## Translating proxies and the `wire:` override (gh-1624)

The boot-time binding preflight validates model ⇄ dialect ⇄ endpoint
(`ProviderModelBinding.resolve`). The vendor-prefix verdict
(`zai/glm-5.3` naming the `zai` record) and the family verdict
(`claude-*`/`gpt-*`/`gemini-*` ids) fire ONLY on known catalog endpoints
(api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) — that is where a dialect
mismatch fails the boot. On unknown/private endpoints the `vendor/`
prefix is treated as a routing key, not a dialect declaration: a
mismatch boots with a `warning: binding — …` line instead of exit 64.
Translating proxies (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api — one host serving
several dialect paths such as `/anthropic` and `/v1`) need no extra
configuration since gh-1624.

`wire:` (the `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` key, the custom-provider and role
surfaces) declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks, overriding the
provider record's own kind. Caveat: the override engages ONLY when the
declared wire DIFFERS from the record's own kind — `record anthropic +
wire: anthropic` changes nothing and the checks still run. The override
silences the dialect checks entirely (the caller asserts the endpoint
speaks it) and is echoed in every binding report (`wire override:`) so
a silenced check is never invisible.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. ### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.

# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

### Fix

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).

# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

blocks.text:
# half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage
          test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart
          test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash
# base64 twin form (identical boot):
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64=$(printf '%s' "$FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG" | base64)
ZAI_API_KEY_BASE64=$(printf '%s' "$ZAI_API_KEY" | base64)
```

`wire` is optional and declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks
(`openai-completions`, `anthropic`, `google`, …), overriding the provider
record's own kind. **Translating proxies** (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api:
one host serving several dialect paths, `vendor/model` prefixes used as
routing keys) need nothing extra since gh-1624 — a `vendor/`-prefixed
model whose prefix names another dialect boots with a warning on
unknown/private endpoints instead of refusing to start. Only real vendor
endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) still fail fast on a
dialect mismatch. The `wire:` override engages ONLY when it differs from
the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash
# bifrost's anthropic path translating zai/glm-5.3 (no wire: needed):
FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{"baseUrl":"http://192.168.1.23:8080/anthropic","model":"zai/glm-5.3","apiKeyEnvVar":"BIFROST_KEY"}'
```

GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged

```bash
# base64 twin form (identical boot):
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64=$(printf '%s' "$FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG" | base64)
ZAI_API_KEY_BASE64=$(printf '%s' "$ZAI_API_KEY" | base64)
```

`wire` is optional and declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks
(`openai-completions`, `anthropic`, `google`, …), overriding the provider
record's own kind. **Translating proxies** (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api:
one host serving several dialect paths, `vendor/model` prefixes used as
routing keys) need nothing extra since gh-1624 — a `vendor/`-prefixed
model whose prefix names another dialect boots with a warning on
unknown/private endpoints instead of refusing to start. Only real vendor
endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) still fail fast on a
dialect mismatch. The `wire:` override engages ONLY when it differs from
the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash
# bifrost's anthropic path translating zai/glm-5.3 (no wire: needed):
FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{"baseUrl":"http://192.168.1.23:8080/anthropic","model":"zai/glm-5.3","apiKeyEnvVar":"BIFROST_KEY"}'
```

GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged

`wire` is optional and declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks
(`openai-completions`, `anthropic`, `google`, …), overriding the provider
record's own kind. **Translating proxies** (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api:
one host serving several dialect paths, `vendor/model` prefixes used as
routing keys) need nothing extra since gh-1624 — a `vendor/`-prefixed
model whose prefix names another dialect boots with a warning on
unknown/private endpoints instead of refusing to start. Only real vendor
endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) still fail fast on a
dialect mismatch. The `wire:` override engages ONLY when it differs from
the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash

FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{"baseUrl":"http://192.168.1.23:8080/anthropic","model":"zai/glm-5.3","apiKeyEnvVar":"BIFROST_KEY"}'
```

GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing

blocks.text:
```bash
# base64 twin form (identical boot):
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64=$(printf '%s' "$FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG" | base64)
ZAI_API_KEY_BASE64=$(printf '%s' "$ZAI_API_KEY" | base64)
```

`wire` is optional and declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks
(`openai-completions`, `anthropic`, `google`, …), overriding the provider
record's own kind. **Translating proxies** (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api:
one host serving several dialect paths, `vendor/model` prefixes used as
routing keys) need nothing extra since gh-1624 — a `vendor/`-prefixed
model whose prefix names another dialect boots with a warning on
unknown/private endpoints instead of refusing to start. Only real vendor
endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) still fail fast on a
dialect mismatch. The `wire:` override engages ONLY when it differs from
the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash
# bifrost's anthropic path translating zai/glm-5.3 (no wire: needed):
FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{"baseUrl":"http://192.168.1.23:8080/anthropic","model":"zai/glm-5.3","apiKeyEnvVar":"BIFROST_KEY"}'
```

GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

`wire` is optional and declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks
(`openai-completions`, `anthropic`, `google`, …), overriding the provider
record's own kind. **Translating proxies** (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api:
one host serving several dialect paths, `vendor/model` prefixes used as
routing keys) need nothing extra since gh-1624 — a `vendor/`-prefixed
model whose prefix names another dialect boots with a warning on
unknown/private endpoints instead of refusing to start. Only real vendor
endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) still fail fast on a
dialect mismatch. The `wire:` override engages ONLY when it differs from
the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash

```

GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing

{"content":"### Root Cause

- gh-1570's binding preflight (`_validateModelEndpoint` in `lib/src/model_roles/provider_model_binding.dart`) made a vendor-prefix dialect disagreement fatal on **any** endpoint. On translating proxies (bifrost/LiteLLM/one-api) the `vendor/` prefix is a routing key, not a dialect declaration — so `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic` + bifrost's `/anthropic` path + `zai/glm-5.3` exited 64 on every boot (1.0.576 regression).

### Fix

- `provider_model_binding.dart`: the vendor-prefix verdict is scoped to **known catalog endpoints**, mirroring `_validateWireEndpoint`'s "unknown endpoints pass" rule — real vendor endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) keep the gh-1570 fail-fast; unknown/private endpoints carry the mismatch as a new `ProviderModelBinding.warnings` note instead of exit 64.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`: the boot notice renders binding warnings (`warning: binding — …`) on the FA_PROVIDER_* path.
- Docs: `wire:` documented with its equal-kind caveat (override engages only when it differs from the record's own kind) in README (env preconfig), `docs/agents/providers.md` (§ Translating proxies), `--help`; CHANGELOG entry marks gh-1570 breaking for proxy factories with the `wire:` migration.

### Test Coverage

- `test/model_roles/provider_model_binding_test.dart`: new gh-1624 REG group — AC1 (unknown endpoint + mismatched prefix boots with warning), AC2 (same mismatch on known vendor endpoints still fatal; family verdict intact), AC3 (`wire:` != record kind skips the checks; `wire:` == kind does not; warnings are not identity).
- `test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart`: the incident `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` now parses with a binding warning; known-endpoint mismatch still dies at parse.
- `test/model_roles/bifrost_proxy_binding_test.dart` (new IT): a bifrost-shaped loopback proxy (anthropic-dialect `/anthropic` path translating `zai/glm-5.3`) boots through `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` and completes a streamed request via the production `providerStreamFunction('anthropic', …)` — proxy saw `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`, and the translated model id.
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): passing.

### Notes

- The family-exclusive check already passed unknown endpoints; unchanged. Queue entries with explicit private baseUrls stop exit-64ing the same way (no code path change needed there).
- `wire:` remains a `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`-level key; the error texts already pointed at it, now it is documented.

With `?wire: wire` as a map entry: `?key` marks a null-aware KEY — key 'wire' is never null, so the entry IS added... with value `wire` which may be null. Hmm, actually `?wire: wire` means "skip the entry if the KEY (wire-as-key?) is null"... no — `?wire: wire`: the `?` applies to the key expression `wire` (the variable), not the string 'wire'. The key expression is the VARIABLE `wire` (which is null when unset!) — so when wire == null, the entry is SKIPPED (key null → skip). When wire != null, key becomes the wire VALUE (e.g. 'anthropic') mapping to 'anthropic' — wrong shape: `{"anthropic": "anthropic"}`. That's why test 3 failed: it expected wireOverride false + warning, got unknown... whatever. Fixed now with `'wire': ?wire` and re-verified standalone 3/3.

So: if the background suite ran the IT after my fix (it started before the fix, but the file is compiled per-suite at load time — the suite loaded it at start, with the ORIGINAL correct `if (wire != null) 'wire': wire` version — which was passing 3/3 before the lint fix). `wire` is optional and declares the adapter kind the endpoint speaks
(`openai-completions`, `anthropic`, `google`, …), overriding the provider
record's own kind. **Translating proxies** (bifrost, LiteLLM, one-api:
one host serving several dialect paths, `vendor/model` prefixes used as
routing keys) need nothing extra since gh-1624 — a `vendor/`-prefixed
model whose prefix names another dialect boots with a warning on
unknown/private endpoints instead of refusing to start. Only real vendor
endpoints (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, …) still fail fast on a
dialect mismatch. The `wire:` override engages ONLY when it differs from
the provider record's own kind (`record anthropic + wire: anthropic`
changes nothing — the checks still run).

```bash
# bifrost's anthropic path translating zai/glm-5.3 (no wire: needed):
FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{"baseUrl":"http://192.168.1.23:8080/anthropic","model":"zai/glm-5.3","apiKeyEnvVar":"BIFROST_KEY"}'
```

GitHub Copilot is a first-class provider. `/provider copilot` connects a
GitHub account via the device-code flow (open the shown
`verification_uri`, enter the `user_code`) or by pasting an existing
token — the flow works headless too — and the Flutter app offers the same
connect as a sheet. Device-flow OAuth tokens (recommended) are exchanged
